threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'double-decker' instead of just 'the bus' and avoid the numbers like it's some kind of quiz.
Caught the N1 last night, and a guy in a neon parka was arguing with a lamppost. He said it was his ex's fault. Classic South London drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw the wild street party at Hermannplatz - a mix of DJ sets and spontaneous dance-offs among strangers, all under the neon lights.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it’s totally normal to find a full-on techno party in a former factory with no sign outside. Just follow the sound!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the exact taco truck that has the shortest line and the best al pastor at 2 AM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus arguing passionately with the driver about the route. Turns out, he was just trying to get to the nearest taco truck.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the side streets that hold the real charm—tiny bakeries and unmarked bars only locals know.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their overuse of 'de nada' after a simple thank you. In Eixample, locals just nod and move on.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 242 is a reliable option over the busier 38. Welcome to our world of delayed buses and Tube strikes!
The 37 bus driver last night was blasting drum and bass, and half the passengers started dancing in the aisles. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a whole family of ducks waddling down the sidewalk, without a care in the world. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you order a currywurst at 3 AM from a food truck parked right next to a techno club. Talk about late-night Berlin!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a real local knows that the best tacos are at the cart by the park after a Friday night BART mess, not at the trendy spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 Balboa give his spare sandwich to a tourist. Classic Tenderloin moment—grit meets generosity right on that crowded bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the best tapas are at La Rambla. But the real gems are hidden in the little bars around the plaza del Sol.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by their struggle with the metro maps—Sagrada Família still has them wide-eyed while the locals rush by.
